learning_outcomes.text: Identify the hardening mechanisms of industrial alloys.
Implement available mechanisms to meet specifications.
Relate mechanical properties (viscosity modulus, stress, dissipated energy, etc.) under static (creep, relaxation) and dynamic loading, as well as thermal properties of polymers to their structures.
Define structure in terms of morphology, chemical functions and the arrangement of chemical sequences in a macromolecule.
Gain an overview of techniques for characterizing the mechanical properties of metal alloys.
Understand in detail the hardening mechanisms of metallic materials.
Know how to use metal alloys.
Be able to make the right choice from among available metal alloys.
Understand the chemical structure of molecules and their supramolecular arrangement.
Be able to choose a grade of polymer according to the mechanical or thermal property required.
Access calculation tools for predicting the value of certain material parameters from the polymer's chemical structure.

syllabus_topics: Chapter 1: Characterization of mechanical properties of metallic materials
Reminders and complements on tensile testing
Details and methods for selecting hardness tests
The benefits of Charpy impact resilience testing
Microstructural and mechanical effects of solid solutions
Precipitation mechanisms and effect on mechanical properties
Chapter 3: Application to common metal alloys

Part 1: Reminders and supplements on polymerization chemistry, the spatial organization of thermoplastic and thermosetting macromolecules and the thermodynamic and chemical reasons for these organizations
Part 2: Using structure-property reasoning, the role of chemistry and the spatial arrangement of molecules on a set of mechanical properties whose definition and measurement techniques are worked on
Part 3: Same approach for thermal properties of polymers
